meta.task: phase 2 scores-trackB: Track B scored with the Track A scripts (20_scores.py, 21_tariff_effects.py), compared with Track A and the paper

tracks.A: authors' prepared data (UPSTREAM feathers): 1,007 ToU households in clusters 325/295/229/158, NOAA temperatures, authors' tariff dummies
tracks.B: our rebuild: 1,032 ToU households, our NMF run-(a) clusters relabelled to the authors' 0-3 (285/299/299/149; matched-cluster series r = 0.986-0.994, ARI 0.58 on the shared 1,007), ERA5 temperatures, Tariffs.xlsx 'loc' alignment; same model code, seeds and selection rule

meta.paper_values: Fig. 4 medians read off the boxplots (spec section 3) plus an independent reading; tariff claims are qualitative (Sec. VII-C), encoded as claimed signs

attribution_rules.cvae: selected-model difference B - A split into (i) the shift of the whole 50-restart distribution (Mann-Whitney A vs B) = data and (ii) the remainder = restart selection (training randomness). label 'data' if the restart distributions differ (p < 0.05) and the remainder < 1 pooled restart SD; 'data + training randomness' if they differ and the remainder >= 1 SD; 'training randomness (restart selection)' if they do not differ but the selected models differ by >= 1 SD; otherwise 'no material difference'
attribution_rules.gam: deterministic fit: 'data' if the paired day-bootstrap CI of the B - A median difference excludes 0 (scores) or the tracks' 95% CIs do not overlap (effects); otherwise 'no significant difference'
attribution_rules.data_reference: no model involved: any A/B difference is data (cluster membership, tariff schedule)

rebuild_scenario_windows.why: tariff-scenario windows corrected from Low 9-18 / High 39-43 to Low 9-19 / High 39-44 (REPRO_SPEC section 7). Scores and sample diagnostics do not depend on the scenario windows (the sample arrays are bitwise unchanged), so those sections are kept from the phase-2 build; the previous file is outputs/archive_windows_9-18_39-43/comparison_AB.json

claims_that_hold_on_track_B: Fig. 4 RMSE level (root-mean over 48 half-hours): ratio to the paper 0.86-1.12, GAM better in all 4 clusters
Fig. 4 variogram (ordered pairs) in 6 of 8 cells (ratio 0.72-1.21; cluster 2 is 24-28% low)
CVAE too little variance (spread/skill 0.10/0.12/0.14/0.08), GAM too much (1.44/1.55/1.49/1.30); CVAE smooth, GAM erratic, real profiles in between

GAM (windows Low 9-19, High 39-44): Low raises (+3.5/+2.9/+2.8/+31.5% in clusters 0-3) and High lowers (-2.9/-3.3/-3.8/-19.1%) consumption in every cluster, effects confined to the window (max |change| outside 0.0e+00 kWh)

cluster heterogeneity (reproduced): cluster 3's effect relative to clusters 0-2 is Low 8.8-14.8x, High 6.6-10.5x in the data (real blocks) and Low 9.0-11.3x, High 5.1-6.7x in the GAM (paper scenarios)
claims_that_do_not_hold_on_track_B: Fig. 4 energy-score values (correct ES: CVAE ratio 0.63-1.25, GAM 0.39-0.70; no variant matches all 8 cells)
'13% RMSE difference': median-based 23.1% (rel. to CVAE) / 30.0% (rel. to GAM)
CVAE energy score lower than GAM's: CVAE/GAM = 1.65/1.83/1.58/1.72

CVAE tariff direction: selected decoders right in both directions (CI excludes 0) in cluster(s) 1, 3 (in-window Low -5.0/+2.9/-3.6/+41.5%, High +3.5/-5.5/-7.4/-8.0%); across restarts both directions appear in 19/17/1/46 of 50

side effect (partially reproduced): no significant drop before/after real High blocks in any cluster of the data; the selected CVAE's High scenario shows it (pre and post CI exclude 0) in 3 of 4 clusters (pre4 +3.6/-4.6/-8.8/-7.1%, post 45-47 +4.7/-5.4/-8.8/-7.4%), restarts 28/45/45/45 of 50; median correlation of the restarts' paper-High response with real training block 33-44 / 35-46 inserted alone 0.88/0.95/0.88/0.95 / 0.68/0.85/0.62/0.89 (co-occurrence with the longer training blocks)

rebound (partially reproduced): selected CVAE Low rebound (drop in 20-31 and 32-47) in 3 and High rebound (rise in 24-34) in 1 of 4 clusters (Low 20-31: -8.1/-3.7/-4.6/-2.7%, 32-47: -6.4/-0.7/-8.4/-9.2%; High 24-34: +2.2/-4.6/-5.0/-5.3%); restarts Low 32/28/43/18, High 26/6/6/1 of 50; data: significant post-Low drop in no cluster, pre-High rise in cluster(s) 3

trackB_vs_trackA.fig4_scores: CVAE: cluster 0 no material difference; clusters 1 and 3 slightly harder in Track B (the whole 50-restart distribution shifts up 2-7%, significant except cluster-1 VG: data); cluster 2 easier (restart medians RMSE -4%, ES -5%, VG -18%: data, a different and larger cluster, 299 vs 229 households). GAM: cluster 2 lower (RMSE x0.87, ES x0.89, VG x0.76, CIs exclude 1); small significant increases for cluster 0 VG (x1.08) and cluster 1 ES (x1.06); the rest n.s. CVAE/GAM ratios unchanged (all B-A CIs include 0).
trackB_vs_trackA.diagnostics: same verdicts in both tracks; numeric differences small (spread/skill, coverage) or data-driven (roughness ratios follow the observed series)
trackB_vs_trackA.tariff_effects_cvae: restart distributions of the in-window, pre4 and post effects (Mann-Whitney A vs B, all four p > 0.05) indistinguishable in cluster(s) 0; selected decoders, in-window effect and attribution: c0 Low A -2.0% vs B -5.0% (no material difference); c0 High A -0.3% vs B +3.5% (no material difference); c1 Low A +4.8% vs B +2.9% (no material difference); c1 High A -11.0% vs B -5.5% (training randomness (restart selection)); c2 Low A -5.1% vs B -3.6% (no material difference); c2 High A -5.7% vs B -7.4% (data); c3 Low A +62.4% vs B +41.5% (training randomness (restart selection)); c3 High A -23.8% vs B -8.0% (data + training randomness (restart selection)); cluster 3 restart median High effect A -20.4% vs B -14.9% (p = 0.001)
trackB_vs_trackA.tariff_schedule: Track B's tariff file has 6 extra High 35-46 training days (Nov-Dec) and other event days without consumption response. They dilute the measured cluster-3 High effect (data, real blocks): -23.8% with the xlsx schedule vs -28.4% for the same households with the authors' schedule (Track A -28.6%), and plausibly the GAM's High 39-44 effect (-19.1% in B vs -25.2% in A) and the CVAE restarts' High effects
trackB_vs_trackA.conclusion: Under the same criteria Track B gives the same verdict as Track A on 11 of 12 claims; it differs on C_fig4_vg_B. Fig. 4 differences come from the data (cluster composition) and are small except for cluster 2 (variogram 24-28% below the paper in Track B). CVAE in-window tariff effects, Track B vs Track A (8 cells = 4 clusters x Low/High, paper windows Low 9-19, High 39-44): attribution no material difference 4, training randomness (restart selection) 2, data 1, data + training randomness (restart selection) 1; the tariff schedule also dilutes Track B's measured cluster-3 High response in the data.

definitions.scenario_windows_note: Low 9-19 / High 39-44 endpoints inclusive (REPRO_SPEC section 7; slot h = the half-hour ending at h x 30 min GMT); phases 1-2 used 9-18 / 39-43 (outputs/archive_windows_9-18_39-43/). High post4 = 45-47 (3 slots left in the day)
definitions.effect: mean over the 200 samples of (scenario - Normal), then over the 92 test days; kWh per household per half-hour (region mean); pct = 100 x effect / Normal mean over the same slots and days
definitions.ci: 95% percentile bootstrap over test days, B = 2000

Low:in_window.text: direction: Low raises consumption inside the window

High:in_window.text: direction: High lowers consumption inside the window

High:pre2.text: side effect: the fall starts a little before the High window

High:pre4.text: side effect: the fall starts a little before the High window

High:post2.text: side effect: the fall continues a little after the High window

High:post4.text: side effect: the fall continues a little after the High window (slots 45-47: only 3 slots remain in the day; = rebound_post_45_47)

Low:rebound_20_31.text: rebound: after a morning Low, consumption drops in the afternoon

Low:rebound_32_47.text: rebound: after a morning Low, consumption drops in the evening

High:rebound_pre_24_38.text: rebound: a little increase in the afternoon with an evening High (window as specified; overlaps pre4)

High:afternoon_24_34.text: rebound: afternoon increase, window without the 4 pre-window slots

definitions.claim_status: appears = claimed sign and CI excludes 0; weak = claimed sign, CI includes 0; absent = opposite sign, CI includes 0; contradicted = opposite sign, CI excludes 0

data_reference.note: event day minus matched all-Normal days (same day type, +-14 days); real Low/High runs of the continuous series; 95% CI = bootstrap over event days. Track A: authors' aggregates and tariff dummies; Track B: our cluster aggregates (data/power_consump_ours.parquet) with Tariffs.xlsx ('loc' alignment). Differences between tracks are data only (no model).

independent_check.note: own re-implementation (no lib.effects functions): in-block effects reproduce the lib values; morning-Low-only days = every Low run ends by slot 10 and no High; Low-rebound regions 20-31 and 32-47; evening-High days = a High run covering 39-44 (afternoon test only on such days whose slots 24-34 are Normal: {'A': 4, 'B': 4, 'B_authsched': 4}); 'week' = baseline from d-7/d+7 when all-Normal

schedule_vs_households_attribution.note: Tariffs.xlsx ('loc') and the authors' dummies differ on 17 days (6 extra Low 11-34 + High 35-46 days and several extra morning-Low days in Nov-Dec, two Low-all-day days in Mar/May); phase 1 found no consumption response on the extra xlsx event days. Their inclusion dilutes Track B's measured responses; with the authors' schedule our cluster-3 aggregate gives the same High effect as Track A.
